considered.reasoning: All coverage-based archive signals measure the *level* of funding health, which is highly persistent and slow-moving, whereas the mispricing story is fundamentally about news that the distress label is wrong — a state transition. Using a one-year change in the same rollover-gap quantity that produced the archive's best joint profile keeps the economics familiar while testing an entirely different information event, and it should have low correlation with the level-based signals already archived.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Goodwill Impairment Trigger
considered.hypothesis: Goodwill is written down when the acquired business misses its revenue case, so a large goodwill balance relative to book equity combined with falling sales predicts an equity-destroying impairment and a genuine, not accounting, deterioration in solvency.
considered.reasoning: The archive establishes that goodwill-heavy strained firms are the reliable short leg but always measures strain through leverage or cash flow; this instead uses the actual impairment trigger — revenue disappointment — combined with the equity cushion available to absorb the write-down. It is a forward-looking distress mechanism specific to acquired intangibles and is economically distinct from the debt-service and coverage conditioners already tested.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Pure Demeaned Research-Coverage Interaction
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), ZSCORE(SUB(RATIO(MA(oancf, 3), at), RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Debt-service coverage should matter far more for the pricing of firms whose asset base is unverifiable knowledge capital than for firms with tangible collateral, so the priced object is the cross-product of the two centered attributes rather than either level.
considered.reasoning: Every archive interaction multiplies two non-negative ranks, so the long leg mechanically contains high R&D intensity and the result cannot be distinguished from a known single-theme R&D effect; centering both legs removes their main effects and leaves only the interaction, which is what the task actually asks for. If this signal retains meaningful alpha, the conditional mechanism is real; if it vanishes, the archive's alphas are a repackaged R&D-intensity premium and the search should pivot decisively to the goodwill/impairment short leg.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Research Floor Under Peak Indebtedness
considered.hypothesis: A firm that never let its research intensity fall below a high floor even in the year its indebtedness peaked has demonstrated, through revealed behaviour, that its financing constraint was not binding; that demonstrated resilience distinguishes accounting distress from genuine fragility better than any contemporaneous ratio.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the balance-sheet-repair family entirely for a revealed-preference mechanism: the floor of research intensity over three years versus the peak of leverage over the same window, so the long leg contains firms that funded innovation *through* their worst debt year rather than firms that simply look adjusted-solvent today. The failed gen-0 retrenchment signal used noisy one-year growth rates in both legs, whereas floors and peaks are stable order statistics of levels, and coalescing R&D to zero keeps non-reporters at the bottom of the commitment leg rather than dropping them.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Expensing Wedge Between Cash Flow and Reported Earnings
considered.hypothesis: For research-intensive firms the gap between operating cash flow and reported income is dominated by the immediate expensing of investment rather than by accrual manipulation or asset deterioration, so a wide positive wedge identifies firms whose loss-making appearance is an accounting convention rather than cash distress.
considered.reasoning: This avoids book equity entirely, so there is no discontinuity as ceq crosses zero and no mechanical rank jump, while still testing the accounting-versus-real distress split at its source — the income statement versus the cash flow statement. It is economically distinct from the archived divergence signal, which compared cash coverage of liabilities against the retained-earnings stock, because it isolates the contemporaneous flow wedge, and the R&D-intensity leg supplies the interpretation that distinguishes it from the generic accruals effect: the same wedge should carry far more mispricing where the investment is expensed.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Liquidation Floor for Innovators
considered.hypothesis: Creditors of an intangible-heavy firm can look through to only one hard recovery source — current assets — so an innovator whose current assets alone exceed all liabilities has a liquidation floor that makes its distress classification economically empty.
considered.reasoning: Every solvency leg tested so far has been a flow (operating cash flow, burn, rollover gap) or a cash stock; net-current-asset value against total liabilities is a stock-based, Graham-style recovery floor that uses the untouched act variable and should be only weakly correlated with the archived coverage measures. It tests whether the false-distress premium comes from demonstrated cash generation or from downside asset protection, which are economically different claims about why the distress label is wrong.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Own-History Distress Extreme in Research Firms
considered.hypothesis: Cross-sectional distress screens compare firms to each other, but a research-intensive firm sitting at the worst net-indebtedness point of its own five-year history is at a transitory extreme in a financing cycle that funds long-lived knowledge capital, and that transitory strain is over-extrapolated by investors.
considered.reasoning: Firm-relative position in its own distress history is an entirely untested state concept here, and it is economically distinct from cross-sectional strain because it holds the firm's business model, industry and asset structure fixed by construction. The archive repeatedly shows that intangible-heavy firms that *look* strained earn positive alpha; this asks whether the effect is driven by strain relative to peers or strain relative to the firm's own norm, which materially changes how the mechanism should be interpreted and refined.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Goodwill Write-Down Risk Against Term Debt
considered.hypothesis: Goodwill is impaired when the acquired revenue case fails, and the write-down destroys the equity cushion supporting long-term debt; the combination of a large goodwill balance, deteriorating revenue and substantial term debt is therefore a forward-looking marker of genuine solvency deterioration.
considered.reasoning: This revives the impairment-trigger mechanism that the validator rejected for lacking a distress-exclusive variable, now anchored on long-term debt so the conditioner combines the impairment trigger with the claim that the write-down endangers. The archive's most reliable short leg is goodwill-heavy strained firms (t=−3.23), but strain has only ever been measured contemporaneously through leverage or cash flow, whereas this predicts the balance-sheet event itself.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Chronic Loss Years With Research Backing
considered.expression: MUL(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(ib), 0), 5), SUB(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(lt, che), at))))
considered.hypothesis: The distress label is applied to firms with repeated loss years, but within that population the loss has two very different causes — research spending that builds unrecorded capital, or an obligation load the business cannot carry — and only the second is genuine fragility.
considered.reasoning: The multiplier is now a single coherent quantity — the count of loss years in the last five, which is exactly what triggers the distress classification — rather than a second ranked ratio with a mismatched denominator, so the construction is a clean conditioning weight applied to a signed tilt. That tilt contrasts accumulated research against net indebtedness on a common asset scale, so the long leg is chronic loss-makers whose losses are investment-driven and whose net debt is low, while the short leg is chronic loss-makers with no research and heavy net obligations; this is the population split the theme asks for, not a recombination of two archived coverage constructions.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: External Debt Reliance of Research Programs
considered.hypothesis: What makes an intangible-heavy firm genuinely fragile is not the level of its coverage ratio but its dependence on new external borrowing to keep the research program running, because that funding source can be withdrawn precisely when the knowledge capital cannot be pledged or sold.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the coverage-gap leg entirely and replaces it with the *financing flow* — the change in interest-bearing debt — so it is not a transformation variant of the demeaned interaction or the rollover-coverage signal, both of which measure resource stocks or flow levels against obligations. The economic content is the funding source of innovation rather than its cushion: a research-intensive firm that expanded its programme without new borrowing has revealed internal financing capacity, whereas one that borrowed to do so has revealed the opposite, and the failed gen-0 retrenchment signal is not a precedent because it conditioned on R&D *cuts* using two noisy growth rates.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Organic Share of Soft Capital Under Net Debt Strain
considered.expression: MUL(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), COALESCE(gdwl, 0))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Among strained firms holding soft capital, the fraction of that capital which was internally generated rather than purchased determines whether the strain is an artifact: organic knowledge capital is understated on the books and generates cash, whereas goodwill is already capitalized and generates none.
considered.reasoning: The accrual-like earnings-minus-cash-flow leg is removed entirely, so the result cannot be a rediscovery of the Sloan effect; the conditioner is instead net interest-bearing debt over assets, a pure balance-sheet strain measure. The composition leg is also rebuilt as a bounded [0,1] share of soft capital rather than a difference of two independently ranked intensities, which makes it a coherent single quantity, immune to the scale mismatch between a five-year expense flow and a balance-sheet stock, and defined only for firms that actually hold intangible capital of some kind.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Revenue Servicing Capacity of Research Firms
considered.hypothesis: Revenue, not cash flow or profit, is the least manipulable evidence that a research firm's knowledge capital has reached commercial scale, and a large revenue base relative to obligations means the firm can refinance or grow into its liabilities regardless of what its earnings look like.
considered.reasoning: Every conditioner tested so far is a cash-flow, cash-stock or balance-sheet quantity, all of which are affected by the same accounting conventions that create the false-distress problem; revenue-to-liabilities is a commercial-scale measure that is immune to expensing, impairment and accrual choices. It also discriminates within the R&D-intensive population between pre-revenue firms, where the distress label may be genuine, and commercialized innovators, where it is an artifact — a distinction none of the archived signals makes.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Lending Beyond Pledgeable Collateral
considered.hypothesis: Term lenders extend credit against tangible collateral by default, so a research-intensive firm carrying long-term debt far in excess of its tangible asset base has been underwritten on the strength of knowledge assets that lenders verified and the balance sheet omits.
considered.reasoning: This is a stock-based collateral-adequacy measure rather than the archived one-year financing flow, and the scaling by tangible assets is the point: it identifies borrowing that could only have been approved on unrecorded asset value, which is the certification mechanism the flow signal could only hint at. The economics are testable and distinct — the same excess of debt over collateral is unambiguously bad for a firm without knowledge capital, so the intangible gate is doing real conditioning work rather than re-signing an archived product.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Composition Tilt Under Multi-Channel Distress Screen
considered.expression: MUL(SUB(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at))), SUMRANK(RATIO(lt, at), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(re, at)), NEG(RATIO(MA(oancf, 3), lt)))))
considered.hypothesis: Misclassification severity rises with the number of independent screens a firm fails — leverage, accumulated deficit and cash coverage — so the organic-versus-acquired composition should be most strongly priced among firms that look distressed on all three channels simultaneously.
considered.reasoning: The internal inconsistency the critic identified is resolved by settling on the direction the archive actually supports: composition tilt earns positive alpha when interacted with *greater* strain (0.064 at t=4.46 with the debt-service gap, 0.059 at t=5.37 with leverage), so the conditioner here is unambiguously a severity score with all three channels oriented so that higher means more distressed. Aggregating three screens by nested rank sums also produces a smoother, better-dispersed conditioner than any single ratio, which is where the archive's flat FMB slopes have come from.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Double Leverage Fragility
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), MA(oancf, 3))))
considered.hypothesis: A high gross margin means a cost structure dominated by fixed intangible investment — brand, research, organization — so operating leverage is high; combining that with debt large relative to recurring operating cash flow compounds the two leverages and creates genuine, not accounting, fragility.
considered.reasoning: The gen-1 gross-margin signal was proposed with a positive sign and delivered a decisively wrong-signed slope (fmb −2.57), which is direct evidence that margin-based intangible proxies interact with distress in the *opposite* direction to research-based ones; this proposal states that finding as an operating-leverage mechanism rather than a hidden-capital mechanism and orients the sign accordingly. Scaling debt by operating cash flow rather than assets makes the conditioner a genuine debt-servicing burden, and the construction reuses the archive's most broadly covered inputs, so any result is not a sparse-sample artifact.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Research Program Longevity Under Net Debt Strain
considered.hypothesis: An uninterrupted five-year record of research spending identifies an established innovation programme rather than a speculative one-off, and such firms carry accumulated, still-productive knowledge capital that makes a strained net-debt position an accounting rather than an economic problem.
considered.reasoning: Every archived intangible gate has been an *intensity* level, which conflates cash-burning start-ups with mature research firms; reporting persistence is an orthogonal attribute — program maturity — and it retains the cross-sectional intangible theme that the firm-relative proposal wrongly discarded. It should also produce a more stable portfolio composition than intensity ranks, since the count changes slowly, addressing the turnover concern that accompanies annually re-ranked intensity gates.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Realized Goodwill Impairment With Leverage
considered.hypothesis: A goodwill write-down is the moment accounting concedes that acquired intangible value never existed; when it lands on a levered balance sheet it destroys the equity cushion supporting the debt, and investors underreact to the resulting deterioration in genuine solvency.
considered.reasoning: This is an event-based mechanism — a realized reduction in the goodwill balance — rather than the level-based goodwill legs already archived, so it is not the monotone negative of the acquired-intangible debt-service signal and its outcome is not known in advance. It also completes the run's asymmetric picture: organic knowledge capital is understated and rewarded, whereas acquired capital is overstated until it is written off, and the write-off is the observable moment when genuine fragility is revealed.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Composition Tilt Under Commercial Scale
considered.expression: MUL(SUB(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at))), RANK(RATIO(sale, lt)))
considered.hypothesis: The organic-versus-acquired composition of soft capital is priced most strongly among firms whose revenue base is large relative to their obligations, because there the knowledge capital has demonstrably reached commercial scale while the goodwill has demonstrably not.
considered.reasoning: This crosses the archive's largest-alpha leg (composition tilt, t up to 5.37 but slopes near zero) with its only conditioner that delivered a strong slope and a solid alpha simultaneously, which is precisely the metric-disagreement the objective asks us to resolve. Unlike the gen-5 multi-channel screen that inverted, the conditioner here is a health measure rather than a mixture of leverage strain and cash-flow failure, so its expected direction is internally consistent with the revenue-servicing result rather than in tension with it.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Chronic Cash Burn in Research Firms
considered.hypothesis: Repeated years of negative operating cash flow, unlike leverage or reported losses, cannot be an accounting artifact — it is the one distress marker that identifies research-intensive firms whose knowledge capital is not yet, and may never be, self-sustaining.
considered.reasoning: The run has established the false-distress side thoroughly but has never isolated the genuine-fragility side within the intangible population, and the gen-5 inversion implies it exists and is driven by cash-flow failure rather than by balance-sheet strain. Counting cash-burn years over five years is a hard, non-accrual, persistence-based criterion, and a reliably negative alpha here would complete the theme's core claim by showing that the same intangible gate produces opposite signs depending on which distress channel it is crossed with.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Growing Into Obligations
considered.hypothesis: An innovator whose revenue base is expanding faster than its obligations is deleveraging through commercialization, so its current distress ratios are a snapshot of a rapidly improving position rather than a stable state.
considered.reasoning: Rather than re-scaling the same static commercial-scale numerator, this changes the economic object from level to *relative rate*: the race between revenue and liabilities, which is what determines whether today's leverage will still bind next year. It is also immune to the gross-profitability rediscovery concern because neither leg is a profitability measure, and the difference of two growth rates is centred near zero rather than inheriting the level of either.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Conjunction of Leverage and Cash Coverage
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(lt, at)), RANK(RATIO(MA(oancf, 3), lt))))
considered.hypothesis: The mispriced population is the conjunction — research firms that are simultaneously heavily obligated and comfortably servicing those obligations from operations — because that is exactly the group a leverage-based screen flags and a cash-flow test exonerates.
considered.reasoning: The rank sum genuinely failed to compute the stated hypothesis, since it scores a safe unlevered firm identically to a strained one; taking the minimum of the two rank legs makes the conditioner high only when *both* conditions hold, which is the correct operator for a conjunction and is untested in this archive. This also removes the objection that the signal loads positively on raw leverage: leverage alone now contributes nothing, because a high-leverage firm with weak coverage is floored by its coverage rank.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Research Spending Against Failing Reported Coverage
considered.hypothesis: A firm that devotes a large amount relative to its obligations to research while reporting weak earnings coverage is not failing to service its debts — it is choosing to spend the coverage on investment, and the reported ratio measures the choice rather than the capacity.
considered.reasoning: The level ratio collapsed to pretax-earnings-over-liabilities because the R&D add-back is zero for most firms; here the research term is the entire first leg rather than a small additive correction, so the intangible channel cannot be swamped. Crucially the profitability leg enters *inverted* — weak reported coverage scores high — so a positive result cannot be the standard profitability or Altman-composite effect, which would predict the opposite; it can only come from the interaction the theme posits.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Tangible Net Worth Coverage
considered.hypothesis: Lenders write covenants on tangible net worth — assets excluding goodwill, less liabilities — because goodwill provides no recovery; firms whose reported equity cushion evaporates once goodwill is removed carry genuine, understated solvency risk.
considered.reasoning: The previous scaling was mis-specified, rewarding acquisitive firms with little debt; expressing the quantity as the covenant definition of tangible net worth over assets makes goodwill and liabilities both reduce the score, which matches the hypothesis exactly and cannot be high for a low-debt acquirer. It is continuous, broadly covered and orders firms from goodwill-inflated, levered balance sheets at the bottom to genuinely asset-backed firms at the top, giving the short leg the same functional form that has produced the archive's strongest cross-sectional slopes.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Multi-Year Coverage Trajectory of Innovators
considered.hypothesis: For research firms the relevant solvency information is the direction the coverage ratio has been travelling for years, not its level in a single year, because a sustained upward trajectory is evidence that the knowledge capital is progressively converting into debt-servicing capacity.
considered.reasoning: The one-year change version earned a 0.039 alpha at t=3.09 but only a 1.29 slope, consistent with a genuine effect measured with too much noise; a five-year fitted trend is a far more precise estimate of the same state variable and is the one temporal construction the archive has never used. Because a trend is centred near zero and roughly symmetric, it should also produce the dispersed, monotone conditioner that the strong-slope signals share.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Brand Capital Servicing Capacity
considered.hypothesis: If the false-distress mechanism is really about expensed intangible investment rather than about R&D-intensive industries, then accumulated advertising — the other major expensed intangible — should show the same premium when paired with commercial scale relative to obligations.
considered.reasoning: The archive's best joint result rests entirely on R&D, and the failed gross-margin experiments left open whether the effect is an intangible-accounting phenomenon or a research-industry phenomenon; substituting advertising capital for research capital in the exact winning structure is the decisive external-validity test. A positive result would broaden the mechanism to consumer and media firms and materially strengthen the economic interpretation, while a null would justify concentrating the final generation exclusively on research capital.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Demeaned Research and Commercial Scale Interaction
considered.hypothesis: Revenue relative to obligations should carry different pricing information for a firm whose asset base is unverifiable knowledge capital than for a tangible-asset firm, so the priced object is the cross-product of the two centred attributes rather than either level.
considered.reasoning: The additive form was correctly criticised for giving half its weight to the standalone R&D-intensity anomaly; centring both legs removes their main effects entirely, so a surviving result is attributable only to the interaction. The same diagnostic applied to the coverage conditioner survived with fmb 2.20 and alpha 0.038, and applying it to the archive's best joint conditioner (revenue-to-liabilities, fmb 3.51, alpha 0.044) is the decisive test of whether that headline result is an interaction or a sum of two known effects.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Triple Conjunction of Innovation, Leverage and Coverage
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(lt, at)), RANK(RATIO(MA(oancf, 3), lt))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm is a false-distress case only if all three conditions hold at once — it holds knowledge capital, it is heavily obligated, and it services those obligations comfortably from operations — and failing any single condition disqualifies it regardless of how strongly the others hold.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the organic-minus-acquired tilt entirely rather than bolting a fifth conditioner onto it, and replaces the multiplicative form with a strict conjunction, which is the correct operator for a hypothesis stated as a set of necessary conditions and is untested in this archive. The nested minimum makes the interaction irreducible — no combination of two strong channels can compensate for a weak third — which is a materially stronger claim than any archived product and cannot be replicated by any linear or bilinear combination of the legs.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Net Unrecorded Backing per Dollar of Obligations
considered.hypothesis: The relevant quantity for reclassifying distress is the net unrecorded asset backing behind each dollar of obligations — accumulated research that the books omit, less goodwill that the books overstate — and firms with high net backing are solvent by an economic standard their reported ratios never capture.
considered.reasoning: Removing total assets from the expression eliminates the (at−lt)/at leverage skeleton that dominated the previous version, so the numerator now contains *only* the two accounting corrections and the denominator only the obligations they must support. It remains a single continuous quantity — the construction class responsible for every strong slope in the archive — while its tails naturally separate research-rich, low-debt firms from goodwill-heavy, levered ones, which is where the archive's reliable alphas have always come from.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Acquired Equity Without Earned Profits
considered.hypothesis: A firm whose asset base is largely purchased goodwill while its accumulated retained earnings are thin or negative has never demonstrated that it can generate profit internally; its apparent scale was bought with external capital, so its solvency rests entirely on an intangible that cannot be recovered.
considered.reasoning: Both legs are stock levels rather than one-year changes, so the signal cannot be a restatement of the asset-growth or net-debt-issuance anomalies that contaminated the acquisition-event version. The pairing of goodwill intensity with the accumulated-earnings channel is untested in the archive — every prior goodwill signal used leverage, cash-flow or revenue conditioners — and it isolates the specific genuine-fragility case the theme requires: soft capital that was bought rather than built, held by a firm with no internal profit history to fall back on.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Net Backing Against Net Obligations
considered.hypothesis: What unrecorded knowledge capital must cover is obligations net of the cash already on hand, floored at the debt actually maturing, since cash-rich firms face no solvency question on the portion of liabilities their balances already extinguish.
considered.reasoning: Scaling by gross liabilities overstates the burden for cash-rich innovators and understates the urgency for firms whose obligations are near-term, so this refines the denominator to the economically binding quantity while the MAX floor prevents the sign inversions and explosions that a cash-rich firm's negative net debt would otherwise cause. It is an economics-driven denominator change to the archive's best signal, not a rescaling for its own sake, and it tests whether the cash cushion belongs in the solvency comparison or is already priced.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Economic Net Worth per Dollar of Obligations
considered.hypothesis: A firm's true equity backing for its obligations is what it has earned and retained, plus what it has invested in research and expensed, minus what it paid above fair value in acquisitions; that single quantity is the complete restatement the false-distress story requires.
considered.reasoning: This unites the archive's best portfolio leg with its strongest correctly-signed slope channel — accumulated retained earnings, which produced −3.26 when crossed with goodwill — into one coherent economic quantity rather than a product of ranked legs. Because all three components are equity-like and enter additively in dollars before scaling, the construction is dimensionally consistent and avoids the mismatched-denominator problem that has weakened earlier composites.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Knowledge Backing of Uncovered Obligations
considered.expression: RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), MAX(SUB(lt, SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0))), dlc)))
considered.hypothesis: Knowledge capital only matters for solvency to the extent that obligations exceed what tangible assets already cover, so the economically relevant comparison is hidden backing against the *uncovered* portion of liabilities rather than against liabilities in total.
considered.reasoning: This is not a transform of the archived level: the denominator changes from gross liabilities to the collateral shortfall — liabilities in excess of tangible assets, floored at maturing debt — which reorders the cross-section substantially because two firms with identical liabilities but different tangible bases now score very differently. The economics are the credit analyst's actual question, namely what must the unrecorded asset cover once the pledgeable base is exhausted, and the floor at short-term debt prevents sign inversions for firms whose tangible assets already exceed all obligations.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Backing Against Financial Debt Only
considered.hypothesis: Operating liabilities such as payables and accruals roll over with the business and do not trigger default, so the obligations that make an intangible-heavy firm genuinely fragile are its interest-bearing debts, and hidden knowledge capital should be measured against those alone.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the differencing that mechanically imported the asset-growth and debt-issuance anomalies and instead sharpens the denominator to the claims that can actually force insolvency, a distinction none of the archive's liability-scaled signals has drawn. Flooring the denominator at cash holdings encodes the economic statement that a firm whose cash exceeds its debt has no financial obligation problem at all, which also prevents the tiny-denominator explosions that made earlier raw ratios outlier-driven.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Goodwill Claimed Beyond Cash Realized
considered.hypothesis: Goodwill is the capitalized promise of future cash flows from an acquisition; when a firm's goodwill intensity ranks far above its actual cash-generating intensity, the promise has not been realized and the carrying value is an impairment waiting to happen.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the retained-earnings leg — itself a documented distress-quality anomaly with the same sign — with the operating cash flow the acquired assets were supposed to produce, so the signal measures corroboration of an accounting claim rather than restating a known quality metric. The bounded rank difference keeps both tails informative and defined for all firms, and it directly implements the run's central asymmetry: organic capital is understated and must be added back, acquired capital is overstated and must be validated against cash.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Unrecognized Research Capital Against Obligations
considered.hypothesis: Only the portion of accumulated research that never reached the balance sheet is genuinely hidden; identifiable intangibles already recognized as assets are visible to every screen, so subtracting them isolates the true accounting blind spot per dollar of obligations.
considered.reasoning: This is not an ablation of the champion's goodwill leg but an accounting correction to its numerator: capitalized development costs and acquired technology sitting in identifiable intangibles are double-counted when the full research stock is added back, which biases the measure exactly for firms that capitalize aggressively. Removing them makes the numerator the genuinely unrecognized asset and gives a sharper test of whether the premium comes from information that is truly off the books rather than from research intensity per se.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Economic Net Worth Against Financial Debt
considered.expression: RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), MAX(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)))
considered.hypothesis: True equity backing — earned and retained profits plus expensed research minus purchased goodwill — should be measured against the obligations that can actually force default, namely interest-bearing debt net of the cash already available to retire it.
considered.reasoning: The two frontier signals differ in exactly one place each: the numerator that produced the archive's best slope (4.60) was scaled by total liabilities, while the denominator that produced the best alpha (0.067) was paired with a sparser numerator; crossing them is the single highest-value test remaining because the deficiencies are complementary rather than overlapping. The retained-earnings term populates the numerator for the majority of firms that report no research, eliminating the tie mass that flattens the champion's slope, while the financial-debt denominator preserves the tail separation that generates the alpha.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Hidden Backing With Cash-Coverage Tiebreak
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), MAX(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)), RATIO(MA(oancf, 3), lt))
considered.hypothesis: Hidden asset backing determines which firms are misclassified, but for the majority of firms that hold neither research capital nor goodwill the measure is silent, and among those firms demonstrated cash servicing capacity is what separates real from apparent distress.
considered.reasoning: The champion's flat slope is a construction problem with a specific cause — a numerator of exactly zero for the large block of firms reporting no R&D and no goodwill, which produces a tie mass that no linear regression can exploit — and adding a second ranked channel that is defined for every firm resolves those ties without disturbing the ordering at the informative extremes. Unlike the earlier three-channel additive score, neither component here is a standalone intangible-intensity measure: the first is a cross-theme backing ratio and the second a cash-coverage ratio, so the composite retains cross-theme content throughout its range.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Restatement Magnitude Relative to Reported Net Worth
considered.expression: RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), MAX(SUB(at, lt), ADD(dltt, dlc))))
considered.hypothesis: The degree to which a firm is misclassified depends on how large the accounting correction is *relative to the reported net worth being corrected*: a research stock worth a fraction of book equity changes nothing, while one comparable to book equity means the reported balance sheet describes a different firm.
considered.reasoning: Adding cumulative cash flow to the numerator would have buried the intangible term under a documented cash-flow-coverage effect, so instead the numerator here is *only* the restatement, and the denominator becomes the reported equity it corrects — a different economic question from every obligations-scaled member of the family. Flooring the denominator at interest-bearing debt prevents the sign inversions and explosions that thin or negative book equity would otherwise cause, while preserving the ordering for the great majority of firms.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Conjunction of Hidden Backing and Cash-Corroborated Acquisitions
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), MAX(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), RANK(SUB(RATIO(MA(oancf, 3), at), RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm qualifies as falsely distressed only if both conditions hold — it owns unrecorded research capital large relative to its debt, and whatever it did acquire is corroborated by the cash its operations actually produce — and failing either condition disqualifies it.
considered.reasoning: The additive ensemble was correctly criticised for penalising goodwill twice and for carrying a standalone profitability rank; here goodwill appears exactly once, inside a cross-theme difference against operating cash flow, and research appears exactly once, in the debt-scaled backing leg. The strict conjunction means neither channel can substitute for the other, which is a materially stronger and non-linear claim than any sum of the two archived components and cannot be replicated by reweighting them.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Goodwill per Dollar of Cash Resources
considered.hypothesis: Goodwill is a claim on future cash that must ultimately be justified by the cash the business holds and generates; the more goodwill a firm carries per dollar of realised and available cash, the more of its asset base is an unvalidated promise facing write-down.
considered.reasoning: This is a change of functional form, not a reparameterisation: the archived version was a difference of two independently ranked, asset-scaled legs, whereas this is a single continuous ratio in which the cash resources directly divide the goodwill claim, and the run's evidence is emphatic that ratio forms generate materially larger alphas in this family than rank differences do. Flooring the denominator at maturing debt keeps it strictly positive for chronic cash burners, whose ordering would otherwise invert.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Solvency Rank Displacement Against Financial Debt
considered.expression: SUB(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(SUB(at, lt), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), MAX(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(at, lt), MAX(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))))
considered.hypothesis: The mispricing is caused by the *movement* in a firm's solvency ranking when knowledge capital is capitalised and goodwill removed, not by the level of solvency itself, so the signal should be the displacement between the restated and reported rankings on an identical scale.
considered.reasoning: Abandoning the exhausted denominator-permutation family, this holds the solvency measure and its scaling completely fixed and varies only the accounting treatment, so by construction the signal contains no leverage-level content and can only reflect the restatement — the cleanest possible statement of the theme. The archived displacement signal used total liabilities and omitted goodwill entirely, earning 0.043 alpha at t=3.75 with a 1.43 slope; performing the full two-sided restatement against the debt scaling that has since proven strongest is a substantive upgrade of the mechanism rather than a rescaling of it.
considered.author: proposer

critic_notes.rationale: The "wedge" collapses algebraically to lt·RDstock/(at·(at+RDstock)), i.e. a plain leverage × R&D-intensity product dressed up as a difference, which is still a legitimate and internally consistent interaction to test but far less conceptually novel than the framing implies, and the positive sign rests on an untested assumption that levered R&D firms are misclassified rather than genuinely risky.

The expression selects exactly the population — accumulated-deficit, high-R&D, typically small unprofitable firms — that the distress-anomaly and profitability (RMW) literatures document as *under*performers, so the stated positive expected sign fights both the known evidence and the FF5 benchmark used for the alpha, and the hard indicator zeroes out the majority of the cross-section, leaving a lumpy, low-dispersion signal.

Economically sensible and sign-consistent, but the two rank legs are strongly positively correlated in the data (cash-rich balance sheets are the norm among R&D-intensive firms), so the product will behave close to a doubled-up R&D-intensity/quality score rather than an identifying interaction, and it risks partially rediscovering known R&D-intensity and cash-holdings premia.

Well-constructed and internally consistent — the goodwill leg and the debt-service-gap leg are conceptually distinct, the negative sign matches the expression's natural direction, and using goodwill as the non-redeployable counterpoint to organic R&D is a genuine cross-theme idea, though it partially overlaps documented goodwill-impairment and leverage effects and should be checked for incremental power over each leg alone.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash-Versus-Book Distress Divergence in R&D Firms
critic_notes.rationale: The rank-difference cleanly operationalizes the stated accrual-versus-cash divergence and the R&D scaler is the right conditioning variable, with the main caveats being that xrd/sale is not coalesced (coverage restricted to R&D reporters, which should be verified as intentional rather than a sparsity artifact) and that the difference term may load heavily on generic profitability/accruals.

The conditional logic is coherent and the negative sign matches the expression, but the leverage-growth leg alone is close to the well-documented net-debt-issuance/asset-growth anomaly, so the test must demonstrate that the interaction adds something beyond that known effect, and both one-year growth legs will be noisy.

critic_notes.target_name: Innovation Capital Net of Net Debt
critic_notes.rationale: Once R&D is coalesced to zero for the ~85–90% of firms that don't report it, the expression collapses to (cash − debt)/assets, so the signal is dominated by the well-documented net-leverage/cash-holdings return relations rather than any knowledge-capital interaction, and summing a ~0.05-magnitude R&D term with a ~0.3-magnitude net-debt term guarantees the intangible leg contributes almost no cross-sectional variation.

This is the archived "Internally Funded Innovation Solvency" signal with the product swapped for a rank sum and a 3- instead of 5-year window — exactly the cosmetic functional-form variant the objective warns against, and the additive form also destroys the conditional ("cash-backed innovation") logic the hypothesis claims, since a firm can now score high on solvency alone with zero R&D.

Introducing a genuine second moment (cash-flow volatility × leverage as a default-boundary proxy) interacted with intangible intensity is a substantively new mechanism relative to the levels-only gen-0 set, the negative sign is consistent with the distress-anomaly direction, and the xad/xrd coalesce keeps coverage broad — though the volatility×leverage leg alone is close to Campbell–Hilscher–Szilagyi territory, so the incremental value hinges on the intangible interaction surviving a control for that leg.

The wedge algebraically reduces to (debt/at)·(intan/(at−intan)), i.e. a smooth product of leverage and intangible share, which is economically the same construct as the archived goodwill×debt-burden signal (ls_talpha=−3.23) with `intan` substituted for `gdwl`, and it is numerically explosive for firms where intangibles approach total assets.

critic_notes.target_name: R&D-Adjusted Pretax Income Repair Under Leverage
critic_notes.rationale: Moving the rank-repair construction from the retained-earnings stock to flow profitability is a defensible extension and the leverage conditioning is coherent, but the rank difference between pi/at and (pi+xrd)/at is close to a monotone relabeling of R&D intensity (a known anomaly), so the design must be able to show it is not simply R&D-intensity × leverage; note also the positive expected sign sits in tension with the archived evidence that intangible-heavy levered firms underperform.

Using gross margin as a broad-coverage proxy for unrecorded brand/organizational capital is a legitimate way out of the 5–14% R&D-reporter slice and the false-distress mechanism is coherent, but the construction risks being a distress-tilted repackaging of the well-known gross-profitability anomaly, so it needs to demonstrate incremental power over gross profitability and over the leverage/RE distress legs separately.

critic_notes.target_name: Organic Minus Acquired Tilt Under Debt-Service Strain
critic_notes.rationale: This is a mechanical crossing of two existing archive signals' legs (the organic-minus-acquired composition and the debt-minus-OCF gap) and will be highly correlated with both, but the stock-to-flow conditioner swap is economically motivated, internally consistent in sign, and a defensible attempt to convert a portfolio-only result into joint evidence.

critic_notes.target_name: Identifiable Intangibles Versus Goodwill Under Cash Coverage
critic_notes.rationale: The hypothesis says composition should separate distress "among firms with comparable cash coverage," but multiplying a signed composition score by a positive coverage rank makes the composition effect largest for the *highest*-coverage (least strained) firms — the opposite of where distress binds — and COALESCE(intan,0) conflates non-reporting with genuinely zero intangibles, undermining the claimed coverage advantage.

Sign logic is coherent (cash cushion up, burn down, gated on R&D intensity) and the cash-stock-versus-burn clock is a genuinely different construct from liability-based solvency, though the rank difference is only a loose proxy for a duration ratio and it overlaps materially with the archive's "Internally Funded Innovation Solvency" and rollover-coverage signals.

Netting cash-flow volatility out of earnings volatility within R&D-intensive firms is a well-constructed second-moment divergence that directly operationalizes the theme and is distinct from the archive's level interactions; the main caveats are its kinship to the published accrual-quality/earnings-volatility literature and the fact that the "accounting noise, not fragility" story implies no premium unless one adds an explicit mispricing step to justify the positive sign.

The hypothesis rests on "cash taxes" as third-party verification, but txt is total tax expense including deferred taxes — precisely the accrual-convention-driven line the story claims to escape (txpd would be the right item) — and rank(txt/at) minus rank(pi/at) is largely a mechanical effective-tax-rate measure, re-treading documented ETR/tax-avoidance anomalies rather than isolating hidden profitability.

This is a mean-to-min aggregation tweak on the archive's existing rollover-coverage signal (with the R&D budget silently dropped from the funding requirement), i.e., the kind of cosmetic design-parameter variant the objective warns against, and TS_MIN over only three annual observations mostly adds noise and unstable portfolio turnover rather than a distinct economic mechanism.

This is essentially the archived "Solvency Rank Displacement from Capitalized R&D" with the archived retained-earnings-repair leg bolted on — an additive variant rather than a new mechanism — and the stated justification is technically wrong, since cross-sectional ranks of zero-R&D firms do shift when other firms' capitalized values change, so the difference is not "exactly zero" for them.

Industry-demeaning both legs is the single most informative unexplored diagnostic for this archive, since it directly tests whether the entire family of R&D×distress alphas is a biotech-versus-tangible-industry composition bet, and the construction is clean and coherent with the stated sign.

The level-to-change pivot is a genuine information-event distinction from the archived coverage signals, but the change leg is dominated by the year-over-year change in operating cash flow, so the signal risks being an R&D-conditioned cash-flow-momentum/earnings-improvement effect — a well-known anomaly family — and the dlc term adds little.

This is the archived "Knowledge-Capital Leverage Overstatement" with ceq substituted for at, and the claim that ranking "neutralizes the pathologies of small or negative book equity" is false — lt/ceq flips sign discontinuously as equity crosses zero, so firms whose capitalized R&D pushes equity from negative to positive will jump from the bottom to the top of the adjusted rank and dominate the long leg for purely mechanical reasons.

The impairment-trigger conditioner (revenue disappointment against the equity cushion) is economically distinct from the archived debt-service and coverage conditioners, but the embedded NEG(sales growth) main effect points against the well-documented sales/asset-growth anomaly direction, and gdwl/ceq inherits the negative-equity sign flip, so any measured spread will need careful decomposition.

Centering both legs to isolate the pure interaction is the correct methodological response to the archive's rank-product signals mechanically loading on R&D intensity, and it is a decisive diagnostic — though the reviewer should note that the product is symmetric, so the long leg will pool high-R&D/high-coverage firms with low-R&D/low-coverage firms, and unwinsorized z-scores of skewed ratios will make the extremes outlier- and microcap-driven.

critic_notes.target_name: Persistent Cash Generation Against Persistent Losses
critic_notes.rationale: This is a cosmetic recombination of two archived signals — the rank-divergence construction of "Cash-Versus-Book Distress Divergence" with the R&D-intensity gate and earnings-versus-cash leg of "Expensing Wedge" — differing only by swapping `re/at` for `MA(ib,3)/at` and adding three-year smoothing, and the two ranked legs even use mismatched denominators (`lt` vs `at`), so the "divergence" is not a coherent single quantity.

The diagnosis of the symmetric ZSCORE×ZSCORE product's diluted long leg is legitimate and the non-negative gate does change the functional form materially, but replacing one ZSCORE with a RANK and adding a winsorizer is close to a transformation variant of the archived "Pure Demeaned Research-Coverage Interaction," and the same gated-rank × coverage-gap structure already appears in "Research Budget and Rollover Coverage."

Net-current-assets-minus-total-liabilities is a genuinely untested stock-based recovery floor (distinct from the archive's cash-flow and cash-stock coverage legs), it uses a previously untouched input, the expected positive sign matches the expression's natural direction, and the construction is simple enough to interpret cleanly — though the leg is correlated with working-capital/liquidity effects that should be checked against known net-working-capital anomalies.

critic_notes.target_name: Own-History Distress Extreme in Research Firms
critic_notes.rationale: Firm-relative (time-series) positioning of net indebtedness is a genuinely new state variable here and economically distinct from cross-sectional strain, but the positive expected sign runs against the well-documented debt-issuance/leverage-increase underperformance, and TS_RANK over five annual observations is a very coarse regressor, so a null or wrong-signed result would be hard to interpret.

critic_notes.target_name: Goodwill Write-Down Risk Against Term Debt
critic_notes.rationale: The impairment-trigger mechanism is coherent and the sign is internally consistent, but it is an incremental respecification of the archived "Acquired-Intangible Debt Service Gap" with revenue decline substituted for the cash-flow gap, and the `NEG(GROWTH(revt,1))` component points in the opposite direction to the well-known low-sales-growth value premium, so the two components of the SUMRANK may partially cancel.

Both legs are already archived, and more importantly `RANK((oancf - ib)/at)` is essentially negative total accruals — the Sloan accrual anomaly — so the archived 0.057 alpha it is being credited with is plausibly a rediscovery, and crossing it with the organic-minus-acquired tilt risks producing a strong result whose source is a published anomaly rather than the false-distress mechanism.

This is effectively the archived "External Debt Reliance of Research Programs" with the NEG removed and dlc dropped, so the archive already reports the answer (the non-negated product earned ~+0.031 alpha at t≈+3.1), making it a sign-flipped rediscovery of the pair's own result rather than a new test.

The organic-minus-acquired leg was already tested against a debt-service *strain* conditioner (gen 2, alpha 0.064, t=4.46) with the same expected positive sign, and the new conditioner is roughly the negative of that strain measure, so the proposal asserts a positive sign for a signal that is largely the reverse of an archived positive result — an internal inconsistency that must be resolved before the recombination is informative.

Reduced to essentials this is a liquidity/inverse-leverage level ratio (current assets over total liabilities) with a modest R&D-stock add-on, which duplicates heavily documented distress/leverage predictors and, as an unranked and unwinsorized raw ratio, will have its Fama-MacBeth slope driven by a handful of tiny-liability outliers rather than by the intangible adjustment the hypothesis is about.

Swapping RANK for TS_RANK on one leg of an archived signal is close to a mechanical variant, and it deletes the cross-sectional intangible-intensity theme altogether, leaving a within-firm investment/financing-expansion timing measure whose expected positive sign runs directly against the well-documented asset-growth and investment anomalies.

NEG(RANK(gdwl))×RANK(strain) is monotonically the exact negative of the gen-0 "Acquired-Intangible Debt Service Gap" (which already delivered −0.044 at t=−3.23), so the outcome is essentially known in advance and, because both legs remain multiplied, it does not isolate the goodwill leg as claimed.

critic_notes.target_name: Revenue Servicing Capacity of Research Firms
critic_notes.rationale: Revenue-to-liabilities is a genuinely different conditioner class from the cash-flow and balance-sheet gates already tried and cleanly separates pre-revenue from commercialized innovators, though it is still a rank product of two individually known predictors (R&D intensity, turnover/inverse leverage) and sits in tension with the archived gross-profit-per-R&D-dollar result that came in negatively signed.

This is a one-token edit of the archive's "Revenue Servicing Capacity of Research Firms" (sale→sale−cogs in the same numerator, same gate, same scaling), i.e. a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the gross-profit leg is additionally a near-direct rediscovery of Novy-Marx gross profitability re-scaled by liabilities.

Both legs are recycled from the archive, but the pairing is a genuine and internally consistent attempt to resolve the documented slope/alpha disagreement (large-alpha composition tilt × the only conditioner with a strong Fama-MacBeth slope), and the signed-difference × positive-conditioner form does behave monotonically in the claimed direction.

The stated target — firms high on *both* leverage and cash coverage — cannot be isolated by SUMRANK, which assigns the same score to a low-leverage/high-coverage firm and a high-leverage/low-coverage firm, so the expression does not compute the hypothesis; separately, loading positively on raw leverage contradicts the distress-risk evidence and is asserted rather than identified.

Because the R&D add-back is zero for most of the cross-section, the signal reduces to pretax-earnings-to-liabilities — an Altman/Ohlson-style profitability-over-leverage ratio and a well-known anomaly composite — so any result will be dominated by the standard profitability effect rather than the intangible-expensing wedge the theme is trying to isolate.

Scaling goodwill by liabilities makes the signal mechanically high for acquisitive firms with *little* debt, which is the opposite of the "illusory asset coverage supporting obligations" story (goodwill/assets or goodwill/equity would match the hypothesis), and the resulting univariate goodwill-intensity sort is close to already-documented goodwill/intangible-intensity effects.

critic_notes.target_name: Chronic Cash Burn in Research Firms
critic_notes.rationale: A defensible and previously untested attempt to isolate the genuine-fragility side within the intangible population using a hard, non-accrual persistence criterion, though the five-valued indicator count is coarse enough to create lumpy, tie-heavy portfolios and it overlaps conceptually with the archive's chronic-loss-years signal.

Nesting SUMRANK gives roughly half the weight to raw R&D-to-assets — a standalone published intangible-intensity anomaly — and the additive form abandons the cross-theme interaction premise entirely, making this a linear repackaging of three already-tested archive legs rather than a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Composition Tilt Under Conjunctive Solvency Screen
critic_notes.rationale: The construction is internally coherent and the MIN conditioner does select the "levered but cash-covering" population as claimed, but this is now the fourth conditioner swap bolted onto the identical organic-minus-acquired tilt leg (leverage, debt-service gap, sales/liabilities, multi-channel SUMRANK), and the prior swaps flipped alpha sign, so the mix-and-match logic of "best slope × best alpha" is exactly the cosmetic-variant pattern the objective warns against.

The quantity is dominated by (at−lt)/at, i.e. one minus book leverage, with two small adjustments, so it is close to a mechanical restatement of a standard leverage/solvency ratio and largely a level-form merge of the already-tested Tangible Net Worth Coverage and Solvency Rank Displacement signals; a winsorized raw level also invites outlier-driven tails.

Replacing a one-year delta with a five-year fitted trend of a different coverage ratio is a substantive measurement-precision refinement rather than a relabeling, the hypothesis matches what the expression computes, and the expected sign follows naturally — though the trend leg overlaps somewhat with generic fundamental-trend signals and should be checked for redundancy with profitability momentum.

Both legs are near-direct proxies for published anomalies — goodwill growth is a component of asset growth/acquirer underperformance and debt change is the net-debt-issuance anomaly — so the interaction is likely to load on Cooper-Gulen-Schill and Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan effects rather than on any new intangible-distress channel.

A genuine and well-motivated external-validity test of whether the mechanism is intangible-accounting or R&D-industry specific, but COALESCE(xad,0) conflates non-disclosure with zero advertising so the first leg will largely rank a disclosure indicator, and the advertising–return relation is itself an established published anomaly, both of which will muddy interpretation of any result.

This is a monotone rank transform of an already-archived signal that by the proposer's own admission leaves the portfolio sort, alpha and Sharpe literally unchanged, so it is a cosmetic re-specification of the Fama-MacBeth regressor rather than a new economic hypothesis.

The net-of-cash denominator with a maturing-debt floor is a genuinely economics-driven change to the binding solvency quantity rather than a rescaling, though the MAX floor makes the denominator discontinuous across the cash-rich/cash-poor boundary and may create a mixed-regime signal whose interpretation is harder than the reasoning suggests.

critic_notes.target_name: Economic Net Worth per Dollar of Obligations
critic_notes.rationale: The construction is dimensionally coherent and the additive-in-dollars restatement of equity is a defensible single quantity, but retained-earnings-to-liabilities is the dominant term and is itself a well-known Altman/distress component, so the test needs to show the R&D and goodwill adjustments add anything beyond a repackaged RE-based distress screen.

Differencing this ratio mechanically converts it into a mixture of R&D-stock growth, liability growth and goodwill changes, so the signal is largely a rediscovery of the debt-issuance/asset-growth and acquisition-underperformance anomalies and overlaps archived goodwill-change and debt-change signals rather than testing the stated repricing-on-news mechanism.

This is the same two ingredients as the archived "Acquired Equity Without Earned Profits" re-expressed as a continuous difference, and the retained-earnings-to-assets leg is itself a documented distress/quality anomaly with exactly the hypothesized sign, so it is simultaneously a within-archive variant and a partial rediscovery.

critic_notes.target_name: Knowledge Capital per Dollar of Obligations
critic_notes.rationale: An ablation of one leg has some diagnostic value, but as a standalone signal R&D stock scaled by liabilities is close to the published R&D-intensity/leverage anomalies and adds no new mechanism beyond what several archived xrd-scaled signals already test.

critic_notes.target_name: Economic Net Worth Against Financial Debt
critic_notes.rationale: A defensible one-factor cross of the archive's best-slope numerator with its best-alpha denominator, but the retained-earnings term will dominate the numerator for most firms, so the result risks being a re-scaled Altman-style RE/debt distress ratio rather than an intangible-restatement signal.

Cumulative five-year operating cash flow will swamp the R&D stock in the numerator, making this largely a rediscovery of the well-documented cash-flow-to-debt coverage/profitability signal with the intangible term as a minor perturbation, which undercuts the stated purpose of isolating the restatement channel.

critic_notes.target_name: Backing Net of Unrealized Goodwill Claims
critic_notes.rationale: This is an additive ensemble of two already-evaluated archive signals that double-penalizes goodwill (subtracted in the first component's numerator and again as a standalone rank) and smuggles in a standalone cash-based profitability rank (oancf/at), so any performance gain will not be attributable to cross-theme content.

Replacing MA(oancf,3) with TS_SUM(oancf,5) inside a rank transform is a cosmetic reparameterization of the archive's existing "Goodwill Claimed Beyond Cash Realized," and the two cash measures will be near-perfectly rank-correlated.

critic_notes.target_name: Knowledge Backing of the Maturity Wall
critic_notes.rationale: This is the fifth denominator permutation in an exhausted family, and the MAX(dlc, che) floor is internally inconsistent with the stated maturity-wall story since for the many cash-rich firms the expression collapses to R&D-stock-over-cash — a burn/liquidity measure, not a rollover measure.

The tie-mass diagnosis (zero numerator for firms with neither R&D nor goodwill) is a genuine and specific construction problem, but the fix is a linear blend with a conventional oancf/lt coverage ratio already used in several archive signals, so attribution of any improvement will be ambiguous.
